answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by clustering identities on correlated behavior: agents that vote, trade, or attest in lockstep — same targets, same timing — are grouped as one vertex in a shared-behavior graph, no matter how many marble-white fresh accounts they spawn. Rewards are then split across the whole cluster instead of paid per identity, so a thousand clones earn no more than one honest agent, while the umber cost of running each clone — compute, fees, latency — keeps eating the attacker's budget. Cloning stops paying.
